candidate.answerReason: The extra 2% tax applies to one eighth of the income, so $28,000 is seven eighths of the income. The total is $32,000.

methods.label: Compare the extra tax
methods.explanation:
Kristin's overall tax rate is greater than \(p\%\), so her income must exceed \(\$28{,}000\). Otherwise, all her income would be taxed at \(p\%\).

Think of her tax as \(p\%\) of all her income, plus an extra \(2\%\) of the part above \(\$28{,}000\). This extra tax also equals \(0.25\%\) of her total income. Since \(2\%\) is eight times \(0.25\%\), the higher-bracket income must be one eighth of her total income.

The remaining seven eighths, or \(87.5\%\), equals \(\$28{,}000\). Therefore her annual income was
\[
28{,}000\div0.875=32{,}000.
\]
This exceeds the bracket threshold, as required. Her annual income was \(\$32{,}000\), choice B.
